Operator:
Good day, and welcome to the CloudForge Q2 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are in listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question and answer session. To ask a question, you will need to press star one on your telephone keypad. There may be a brief pause while we poll for questions. Please be advised that today's call is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Sarah Johnson, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Johnson:
Thank you, Operator. Good afternoon, everyone, and welcome to CloudForge's Q2 2024 earnings call. Joining me today are Alex Rivera, CEO; Jordan Lee, CFO; Taylor Kim, CTO; Morgan Patel, Chief Revenue Officer; and Casey Wong, Chief Product Officer.

Before we begin, I'd like to remind you that this call contains forward-looking statements. Actual results may differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a complete discussion of risks and uncertainties.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Alex Rivera.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you, Sarah, and good afternoon, everyone. I'm pleased to report on CloudForge's performance for Q2. We achieved significant milestones this quarter, driven by strong demand for our CloudForge AI platform and continued execution of our strategic initiatives.

Our focus this quarter was on six key areas: ARR growth year-over-year and quarter-over-quarter, sales efficiency including cycle lengths and conversion rates, LTV to CAC ratio, capital allocation strategy, cash runway and position, and full-year revenue guidance.

These efforts have positioned us for sustained momentum. On ARR, we hit impressive year-over-year and sequential gains through new logos and expansions. Sales efficiency improved with shorter cycles and better conversions across segments. Our LTV/CAC expanded into elite territory, capital allocation stayed disciplined across investments and buybacks, our cash position extended the runway meaningfully, and we're raising full-year guidance based on this strength.

We are confident in our ability to continue this momentum and deliver long-term value to our shareholders.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Jordan Lee to discuss the financials in more detail.

Jordan Lee:
Thank you, Alex. As Alex mentioned, we had a strong quarter. Revenue for the quarter was $132 million, representing a 45% increase year-over-year. Our gross margin was 82%, and operating income was $28 million.

We continue to invest in research and development to drive innovation and expand our product offerings. Our cash position remains strong, providing us with the flexibility to pursue strategic acquisitions and other growth opportunities.

Let me dive deeper into those six key areas Alex highlighted, starting with ARR growth. ARR ended the quarter at $510 million, up 44% year-over-year from $354 million and 7% quarter-over-quarter from Q1. This excludes any meaningful FX impacts. The year-over-year growth came from $55 million in new logo ARR from 180 net new customers, with average ACV rising to $235,000, highlighted by multi-year commitments like a $12 million deal from a top global bank adopting our ForgeAI suite. Net expansion drove dollar-based net retention to 124%, with upsells into Kubernetes tools and security add-ons at 40% attachment rates, while gross dollar churn stayed under 4%. Regionally, North America led with 42% YoY growth, EMEA at 32% to $92 million, and APAC exploding 55% to $51 million on wins in Japan and India e-commerce. Sequentially, new logos added 3 points, expansions 3 points, and pricing 1 point, with large deals over $1 million now 42% of ARR. This acceleration supports our land-and-expand model, with cohorts expanding 150% within 18 months, powered by AI agents automating CI/CD tasks and a partner ecosystem driving 18% of expansions. CAC payback is now 14 months, and we expect mid-30s YoY growth in Q3.

Next, sales efficiency. Our weighted average sales cycle shortened to 112 days in Q2, down 12% quarter-over-quarter and 8% year-over-year. For SMB self-serve under $25,000 ACV, it's 45 days with 60% no-touch closes via PLG and AI nurture. Mid-market at $25,000 to $100,000 ACV holds at 105 days, aided by virtual tools like Zoom-Gong intelligence. Enterprise over $100,000 is 185 days but improving with faster 45-day POCs. North America averages 98 days, EMEA 130 with partner offsets, APAC 150 easing with localized portals. Conversion rates hit 28% end-to-end, up 4 points quarter-over-quarter: MQL to SQL at 32% from AI lead scoring, SQL to opportunity 48% via intent data, opportunity to close 38% with battle card automation winning 65% against rivals. Our Forge Velocity initiative predicts wins at 88% accuracy, MEDDPICC filters low-propensity deals, and partners contribute 22%. This bowtie funnel with 128% NRR fueled $50 million new ACV, and we see cycles below 105 days in Q3.

Turning to LTV/CAC ratio, it improved to 3.8x in Q2, up from 3.4x year-over-year and 3.6x sequentially, our seventh straight quarter of expansion. CAC fell 12% to $11,200 per customer via PLG shifting 40% to self-serve trials, with sales and marketing at 28% of ARR and payback under 14 months. LTV reached $42,600, with ARPU up 9% to $14,500 on 118% NRR from AI upsells penetrating 35% of base, 82% margins, and best-in-class 7% logo churn and 4% revenue churn. North America at 4.2x on fintech/healthcare deals, EMEA 3.6x, APAC 2.9x improving on premium adoption, LATAM 2.7x accelerating. AI predictive churn models cut risk 15%, pushing us to 4.0x by year-end with Rule of 40 at 52.

On capital allocation, we ended with $528 million in cash equivalents, up $18 million sequentially on $22 million operating cash flow. Priorities: 65% or $420 million YTD in organic investments, including $180 million R&D at 22% of revenue for AI like CloudForge Predict forecasting at 95% accuracy, multi-cloud orchestration lifting NRR 15%. Regional returns strong: North America 68% ARR up 25%, EMEA 18% up 35%, APAC 14% with $40 million in verticals. 20% or $130 million in tuck-ins like an $85 million causal AI deal adding $12 million ARR at 150% expansion, targeting 3x ROI. 10% or $65 million in repurchases at 7.2x EV/FCF, and 5% balance sheet with debt paydown. Next 12 months: $600-700 million deployed, targeting 30% FCF margins.

Regarding cash runway, this $528 million gives us 32 months at $20 million quarterly burn, or over 24 months conservatively, ahead of peers. Q2 cash flow up 45% on RPO growth to $1.2 billion, DSO at 52 days, NRR 118% across 2,500 clients. Capex $12 million for data centers, $8 million buybacks under $100 million program. U.S. 72% ARR generates most inflows, EMEA cash-positive, APAC high-growth with $15 million H2 investment. Initiatives: 25% R&D to Copilot at 65% attach, OpEx 82% of revenue via headcount optimization, M&A in cybersecurity with $300 million revolver buffer. Q3 cash flow $25-28 million, full-year FCF $45-55 million, extending to 36+ months toward $500 million ARR FY25.

Finally, full-year revenue guidance. We're raising to $535 million to $555 million, or 42% to 48% growth from $375 million FY23, up from prior $520-540 million. Q2 beat at 45% growth, ARR $510 million on 124% NRR, new ACV $55 million. Subscriptions $510-530 million at 45-50% growth, services flat $25 million. Americas 68% at $365-375 million up 46%, EMEA 22% $120-125 million up 55%, APAC 10% $50-55 million up 65%. Tailwinds: AI optimizer 30% adoption, Kubernetes security up 80%, consumption pricing. Conservatism for H2 new ACV 35-40%, Q3 $138-142 million, full-year op income $140-150 million at 26-27% margins.

We are updating our full-year guidance accordingly.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Taylor Kim for a technology update.

Taylor Kim:
Thank you, Jordan. This quarter, we made significant progress in advancing our AI capabilities and further integrating them into our core platform. We are seeing strong adoption of our new AI-powered features, which are driving increased user engagement and improved customer outcomes. We've also focused on enhancing our platform's security and scalability to meet the growing demands of our enterprise customers.

And now Casey Wong will provide update on product roadmap.

Casey Wong:
Thank you, Taylor. We have been focusing on the user experience of our products and are excited to announce the launch of CloudForge Copilot. This new feature significantly improves natural language BI queries and real-time analytics. We are seeing strong adoption of this feature which aligns with our product strategy.

Now, I'll turn the call back to the operator for Q&A.

Operator:
Thank you. Ladies and gentlemen, if you would like to ask a question at this time, please press star one on your telephone keypad. Our first question comes from Ben Thompson with Morningstar.

Ben Thompson:
Hi, good afternoon. Can you discuss the impact of CloudForge AI on your overall growth, what kind of attach rates are you seeing, and how it compares to your initial expectations?

Morgan Patel:
Thanks, Ben. CloudForge AI has been a major driver, contributing over 25% of Q2 new ACV through upsells and new logos, accelerating overall revenue growth by embedding AI into DevOps workflows for 70% faster pipelines. Attach rates are hitting 65% among existing customers, especially in betas with partners like Salesforce, exceeding our initial 50% target by a wide margin due to the clear ROI in dev velocity and cost savings.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Lisa Chen with Goldman Sachs.

Lisa Chen:
What are your plans for international expansion, specifically in the APAC region, and what are your key target markets?

Alex Rivera:
Great question, Lisa. APAC is our highest-growth area at 55% YoY, representing 10% of ARR. We're allocating $15 million in H2 for go-to-market teams in Sydney and Singapore, building on Tokyo data center for low-latency. Key targets include fintech like Stripe integrations in Japan, e-commerce platforms akin to Flipkart in India, and multi-cloud analytics with AWS/Azure partners, aiming for 20% market share in mid-market via localized pricing and Tencent co-selling.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Mike Rossi with Piper Sandler.

Mike Rossi:
How are you managing churn in the current economic environment, what's the trend you are seeing in NRR, and what are your strategies to improve customer retention?

Jordan Lee:
Thanks, Mike. Churn remains low at 4% annualized revenue and 7% logo, below peers, managed through proactive monitoring and AI tools. NRR is trending up at 118-124%, steady on expansions offsetting any macro softness. Strategies include our predictive churn model using LLMs on telemetry, deployed to 80% of accounts cutting risk 15%, plus Copilot upsells at 35% penetration and partner integrations boosting utilization—cohorts show 150% expansion in 18 months.

Operator:
Thank you. I'm showing no further questions at this time. I'd like to turn the call back over to Alex Rivera for closing remarks.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you for joining us today. We are pleased with our progress this quarter and remain committed to delivering strong results for our shareholders. We look forward to speaking with you again on our next earnings call.

Operator:
Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
